messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: paired boxplot in greyscale
parts:
Hi,

I want to create "paired" boxplots for publications in greyscale.
What I found quite nice is following "stacked/paired" boxplot here:
http://aob.oxfordjournals.org/content/108/1/1/F3.expansion.html
(sorry, but here you need a subscription to the journal. Just to
explain it for the others: The boxplot are partly overlapping per pair to save space on the x axis)

I tried now to re-build that with ggplot2 but there are some
things I don't know how to do them. So far I can do a "paired"
boxplot in colours:

# paired boxplot
#creating sample data and dataframe
group <-c(rep("A",5),rep("B",6),rep("C",4))
x1 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
x2 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
df1 <- data.frame(group,x1,x2)
#reshape dataframe for this approach
df2 <-reshape2:::melt.data.frame(df1,id=c("group"),variable.name="X",value.name="VALUE")


p <- ggplot(df2)+
geom_boxplot(aes(y=VALUE,x=group, fill = factor(X)))+
#scale_colour_grey()+
theme_bw()
p

There are some questions:

1) How can I change the single colours? scale_colour_grey doesn't work in that case?!

2) How can I let the "pairs" overlap (like in the example)? Can that be done with ggplot2?

best regards,
Johannes

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: paired boxplot in greyscale
parts:
Johannes,

You're using a fill so you need to specify that in your scale_*_grey()

ggplot(df2)+
geom_boxplot(aes(y=VALUE,x=group, fill = factor(X)))+

scale_fill_grey(start=0.5, end=1)+
theme_bw()

RE: overlap... I have no idea, but I'll play with it for a while. I
imagine Hadly/Takahashi/Baptiste might have a clue.

Brandin

messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: expression in boxplot labels (dev)
parts:
Hi,

I now realised what was my problem. It is caused
by the dev mode of ggplot2. The example which works
in normal mode but not in ggplot2 dev mode:

#creating sample data and dataframe
group <-c(rep("A",5),rep("B",6),rep("C",4))
x1 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
x2 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
df1 <- data.frame(group,x1,x2)
#reshape dataframe for this approach
df2 <-reshape2:::melt.data.frame(df1,id=c("group"),variable.name="X",value.name="VALUE")

p <- ggplot(df2)+
geom_boxplot(aes(y=VALUE,x=group, fill = factor(X)))+
scale_fill_grey(start=0.5, end=1, labels= c(x1= expression(alpha == 1), x2= expression(beta==1)))+

theme_bw()+
opts(legend.position = "right")

There is an error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) :
class '"expression"' can't be transformed in data.frame??? Maybe the new version needs the input in another form??

Anyway, I am not sure why in normal mode there is also a "problem" with the final plot. First alpha and beta are just a and b (maybe just a setting to get real greek letters) and then the = 1 is somehow shifted... How can I set to get real greek letters? I am working on a Mac (if that is needed as information)

/Johannes

Hi,

--

Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology,
The University of  Tokyo, Japan.
http://www.fennel.rcast.u-tokyo.ac.jp/profilee_ktakahashi.html

2011/11/25 Johannes Radinger <JRad...@gmx.at>:

> Hi,
>
> I now realised what was my problem. It is caused
> by the dev mode of ggplot2. The example which works
> in normal mode but not in ggplot2 dev mode:
>
> #creating sample data and dataframe
> group <-c(rep("A",5),rep("B",6),rep("C",4))
> x1 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
> x2 <- c(runif(5,1,5),runif(6,1,10),runif(4,2,15))
> df1 <- data.frame(group,x1,x2)
> #reshape dataframe for this approach
> df2 <-reshape2:::melt.data.frame(df1,id=c("group"),variable.name="X",value.name="VALUE")
>
>
> p <-    ggplot(df2)+
>                geom_boxplot(aes(y=VALUE,x=group, fill = factor(X)))+
>                scale_fill_grey(start=0.5, end=1, labels= c(x1= expression(alpha == 1), x2= expression(beta==1)))+
>                theme_bw()+
>                opts(legend.position = "right")
>
> There is an error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) :
>  class '"expression"' can't be transformed in data.frame??? Maybe the new version needs the input in another form??
>
> Anyway, I am not sure why in normal mode there is also a "problem" with the final plot. First alpha and beta are just a and b (maybe just a setting to get real greek letters) and then the = 1 is somehow shifted... How can I set to get real greek letters? I am working on a Mac (if that is needed as information)
>
> /Johannes
